title: People missed that Lot hesitated to leave sin even when angels warned him (Genesis 19:16)
paragraphs: People missed that Lot hesitated to leave sin even when angels warned him (Genesis 19:16)

Lot was not dragged out of Sodom because he was strong.
He was dragged out because God was merciful.

“But he lingered…”
That line should disturb us.
The angels warned him. Judgment was near. Fire was coming.
And still… he hesitated. (Genesis 19:16)
That is the insanity of sin.

Sin can make a man sit still in a place God is trying to rescue him from.
It will whisper, “Stay a little longer.”
It will make bondage feel familiar.
It will make danger feel normal.
It will make compromise feel like home.

Lot’s hesitation did not cancel God’s intervention.
“The men seized him… the LORD being merciful to him.”
That is grace. Fierce grace. Interrupting grace. Grabbing-you-before-you-burn grace.

Some people are waiting to feel ready to leave sin.
But sin never loosens its grip by negotiation.
You do not flirt your way out of Sodom.
You flee.
And that’s where the Gospel walks in.

We all have a Genesis 19:16 moment.
Warnings we ignored.
Doors God opened, but we delayed.
Conviction we felt, but resisted.

Yet Jesus steps into our hesitation with mercy.
Not to excuse our sin.
To pull us out of it.

The cross is proof that God does not merely warn sinners.
He makes a way to save them.
Christ took the judgment we deserved, so we could leave the burning city and walk into mercy.

So yes—Lot hesitated.
And many still do.

But the good news is this:
God’s mercy is stronger than your delay, and Jesus still rescues those who stop lingering and surrender.

Don’t camp where God told you to run.
Don’t romance what heaven has condemned.
Leave while mercy is calling.
